subject: Partner runbook: vector store interop & SLA checklist
messages:
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: partnerships@pinecone.io, onboard@weaviate.io, ops@aperturelabs.com
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Partner runbook: vector store interop & SLA checklist

Hi all,

Thanks for the quick sync earlier. Per Aperture's ask, I'm putting a lightweight runbook together that covers Redwood + partner responsibilities for productionizing a vector-backed search pipeline (examples: Pinecone, Weaviate, pgvector fallback to S3). Goal: make the on-call/triage and SLA boundaries clear so Aperture can move from pilot -> Dedicated without surprises.

Key sections attached as a starter: interop-checklist.xlsx (owner matrix), sample_manifest.json (indexing manifest example). High-level items I want aligned on now:
- Data ingestion schema & manifest: who owns schema validation + transformation (Redwood vs partner)
- Indexing SLA: expected time-to-index for new batches and retry semantics
- Query SLA & fallback: latency SLOs for queries and clear fallback path to S3/pgvector if the primary vector service is saturated
- Security/compliance: API key lifecycle, IP allowlists, and audit log access for audits

Aperture is keen on a 99.9% query availability at 100ms p50 for their conversational search workload; we should call out realistic expectations per partner. Marcus/dev — can you annotate the checklist with any known technical constraints (e.g., Pinecone per-request vector dimension limits, recommended batch sizes) by EOD?

Pinecone/Weaviate — can you confirm any required onboarding artifacts (billing/legal aside) and whether you can host a temporary cross-account audit token so Aperture can validate retention settings?

Proposed next steps:
1) Partners confirm onboarding artifacts + any automation hooks (API vs SFTP ingest).
2) Redwood dev writes the S3 fallback design and posts to the shared Drive.
3) Align on a 30-min technical walkthrough with Aperture next week (I propose Wed 04/07 10am PT).

Thanks — Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Head of Partnerships (Americas)
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Partner runbook: vector store interop & SLA checklist

Hi Laura (and team),

Appreciate the clear outline — this is aligned with what we've done for similar enterprise pilots. Quick notes from Pinecone:
- Onboarding artifacts: API key provisioning instructions and a short onboarding checklist (see attached pinecone-onboard.pdf).
- Indexing SLA: we typically quote latency-to-index per batch size; we'll provide a small table matched to the manifest example (batch sizes 100/1k/10k).
- Audit token: we can issue a scoped read-only token for Aperture to validate retention and namespace policies; we need a signed NDA addendum for token scoping.

Questions for Redwood:
- For the S3 fallback, do you want us to return a specific error code so your router can trigger the fallback immediately, or should we serve a 503 that leaves retry behavior to the caller?

We'll loop in technical onboarding next steps when you have the manifest annotated.

Best,
Evan Gomez
Partner Engineering, Pinecone
partnerships@pinecone.io

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 13:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partner runbook: vector store interop & SLA checklist

Laura — quick technical read from my side after skimming the manifest:
- Dimension consistency: Aperture's model uses 3 different embedding dims across pipelines (512, 1536, 2048). We'll need namespace-level validation or dynamic dimension-checking at ingest to prevent silent index failures. Recommend adding "dimension" to the manifest schema and a rejection policy for mismatches.
- Batching & cost: For 1536-dim embeddings, recommend batch size ~500 for throughput cost sweet spot on GPUs; Pinecone's per-request CPU work scales linearly with dimension (they confirmed this in our last pilot).
- S3 fallback: I'm drafting s3-fallback-design.md — plan is: 1) Redwood router detects partner-specific 5xx (we'll define the exact codes), 2) stream index writes into an S3 prefix with idempotent manifests, 3) background worker replays to partner once capacity recovers. This preserves ordering and makes audits simpler.

I'll drop the s3-fallback-design.md into the Drive and attach here for quick review. Marcus — can you add an ops runbook snippet with the exact pager escalation (who to call at Pinecone/Weaviate after-hours)?

-Karthik

Attachments:
- s3-fallback-design.md (markdown)
